description:
Complete the clustered runtime in four phases: connected-BEAM convergence, durable Bedrock-backed singleton failover, keyed fleet hardening, and disconnected-island lease/fencing.

Public contract choices:
- Keep Jido.Cluster.InstanceManager as the stable API surface: get/lookup/call/cast/stop/stats/owner_node.
- Keep one primary per key with optional standby. No same-key multi-master mode.
- Keep ownership and coordination in jido_cluster; keep persistence in Bedrock.
- Keep :connected_beam as the V1 backend. Add {:bedrock_lease, ...} only in the disconnected-island phase.
- Jido.Cluster.Storage.Bedrock is the durable state backend for clustered failover; Bedrock does not own agent placement.
- No distributed worker-pool API is part of this roadmap. The clustered unit stays a keyed singleton, later expanded to a keyed fleet.

Test and acceptance shape:
- Keep using .spec as the current-truth contract layer and update the relevant subject per task.
- Keep fast unit/contract coverage in default mix test.
- Keep heavy real-Bedrock acceptance tagged and excluded by default, but required for the durability tasks.
- Success bar: connected-BEAM heal converges to one primary per key; durable Bedrock-backed failover survives owner loss and restart; many-key fleet behavior is deterministic and state-preserving; disconnected islands use lease/fencing instead of same-key dual execution.

Assumptions:
- This roadmap covers the full plan, not only the next milestone.
- Issue titles in this roadmap are canonical and should stay stable for dependency clarity.
- Same-key multi-master behavior is explicitly out of scope.
title: Jido Cluster Distributed Runtime Roadmap
